title: Vector operations
learningGoals: find a value in a vector

youtube.title: C++ Vector: insert, erase, sort and find | C++ Programming EP 36
youtube.description: In this episode you will insert and erase items, sort a vector and find a value in a vector, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 Vector operations · 0:51 Insert and erase · 1:31 The vector after each call · 2:01 Second program · 3:01 Recap · 3:31 Bug of the Day · 4:19 Challenge · 4:39 Next episode

scenes.animation: Tomato title card: EP sticker thuds in, title stamps with a whoosh, Xecxec scuttles in and waves; thud, whoosh, claw-click, sting
scenes.narration: Today we use the vector toolbox. You will insert, erase, sort and search with only a few lines.

scenes.onScreen: "Vector operations": numbered lines (1. Insert and erase use iterators; 2. begin points to the first item; 3. Sort and find come from the algorithm header) and an analogy card: a train: you can add a coach in the middle, remove one, or re-order them
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: A vector has many tools. Insert adds an item at a position. Erase removes an item at a position. Both use an iterator. The begin function gives an iterator to the first item. The algorithm header adds sort and find. Think of a train. You can add a coach in the middle, take one out, or put them in order.
points: begin points to the first item
Sort and find come from the algorithm header

analogy.title: Vector operations
analogy.body: A train: you can add a coach in the middle, remove one, or re-order them

scenes.onScreen: edit.cpp: insert 99 at position one, then erase the first item
scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right
scenes.narration: [HL 6] The vector starts as ten, twenty, thirty. [HL 7] Begin plus one is the second position. Insert puts ninety-nine there. [TRACK size=4] The vector is now ten, ninety-nine, twenty, thirty. [HL 8] Erase removes the first item. [HL 9] The loop prints ninety-nine, twenty, thirty.

scenes.onScreen: a table: each call and the vector after it
scenes.animation: Table rows slide in one by one; the row the narrator mentions glows butter
scenes.narration: Follow the table. The start is ten, twenty, thirty. Insert adds ninety-nine at position one. Erase removes the first item. Push back adds five at the end. Items move to make room, or to close the gap.

diagram.caption: a table: each call and the vector after it

scenes.onScreen: sortfind.cpp: sort puts the values in order, find looks for one
scenes.animation: Second program or a twist on the first; [HL n] and [TRACK name=value] cues drive the variable tracker; output panel fills line by line with a ding per line
scenes.narration: [HL 8] Sort takes the start and the end of the vector. It puts the items in order. [HL 9] The loop prints ten, twenty, thirty, forty. [HL 13] Find looks for thirty. It returns an iterator to the item. [HL 14] Subtracting begin gives the index. Thirty is at index two.

scenes.animation: Dark-blue terminal: the compile command types with key-tick, the run command types, output prints in mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Save the file as sortfind dot cpp. Compile it with g plus plus. Then run the program. The program prints the sorted numbers, and then the index two.

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One. Insert and erase need an iterator. Two. Begin gives an iterator to the first item. Three. Sort puts the items in order. Four. Find returns an iterator to the match. Pause the video. Say these ideas out loud, one time, slowly.
points: Insert and erase need an iterator.
Begin gives an iterator to the first item.
Sort puts the items in order.
Find returns an iterator to the match.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: Erase with a number
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the g++ error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. We call erase with the plain number one. The compiler says no matching function for call to erase. Erase wants an iterator, not an index. Write begin plus one, and the call works.

scenes.onScreen: I tried to find my lost sock in a sorted vector. It was at the end, as always.
scenes.animation: Full tomato screen, card flips in with a rimshot, Xecxec snaps his claw
scenes.narration: I tried to find my lost sock in a sorted vector. It was at the end, as always.

scenes.animation: Task card pops in; checklist ticks with a pop; Xecxec holds a tiny pen
scenes.narration: Your challenge: Make a vector with five numbers. Sort it, and print the smallest and the biggest. Write your answer in the comments.

scenes.animation: Next-episode card slides up with a whoosh; right side stays empty for end-screen elements; sign-off text types in
scenes.narration: Next time: more string tools. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

bug.error:
Compiler output (exactly as g++ prints it):

edit.cpp: In function 'int main()':
edit.cpp:7:12: error: no matching function for call to 'std::vector<int>::erase(int)'
    7 |     v.erase(1);
      |     ~~~~~~~^~~
bug.why: Erase wants a position in the form of an iterator, not an index. Add the index to begin to make an iterator.

pun: "I tried to find my lost sock in a sorted vector. It was at the end, as always."
challenge: Make a vector with five numbers. Sort it, and print the smallest and the biggest.
challengeAnswer: After sort, the smallest is v front, and the biggest is v back. Print both.
